messages:
jin: Heads-up — Alertmanager fired GPUUnhealthy for node gpu-12 about an hour ago. Seeing repeated Xid errors in DCGM exporter logs and some ECC corrected spikes.

ashley: saw it too. dcgm_xid_errors_total jumped then went quiet. pods got rescheduled but the node stayed Ready.

kevin: do we have the alert rule right now? IIRC we fire immediately on any XID > 0 which is noisy for short spikes.

maria: yup, current rule is aggressive. snippet from prometheus rules: 
```yaml
- alert: GPUUnhealthy
  expr: (dcgm_xid_errors_total > 0) or (dcgm_ecc_uncorrected_errors_total > 0)
  for: 1m
  labels:
    severity: critical
```

ashley: that 1m window is too short, and dcgm exporter sometimes emits a burst on export cycles. We should use rate() and a higher for:.

kevin: suggested tuning: use recording rules to aggregate per-gpu rate over 15m, then alert if sustained. e.g. 
```yaml
- record: job:gpu:xid_rate15m
  expr: rate(dcgm_xid_errors_total[15m])

- alert: GPU_XID_SustainedSpike
  expr: job:gpu:xid_rate15m > 0.001
  for: 30m
  labels:
    severity: page
```

jin: 30m for a page seems long. For pages we care about persistent failures that cause OOMs or driver resets. Maybe two tiers: warning (15m) and page (30m).

maria: agree. Also add a suppression for Xid bursts correlated with driver restarts: detect `dcgm_gpu_reboot_count` (we have dcgm_exporter metric dcgm_driver_restarts_total) so don't double-alert during a known restart window.

ops-bot: alertmanager: GPUUnhealthy on gpu-12 resolved — node still has some corrected ECC events but no uncorrected errors in the last 10m. :white_check_mark:

ashley: operational suggestion: cordon+drain nodes that show repeated uncorrected errors. We should annotate replacement policy: if node has >3 uncorrected ECC errors in 24h or Xid rate > threshold for 6h, mark for replacement.

kevin: +1. We should also ensure kube-scheduler tolerations and node-affinity for low capacity windows. When we drain a GPU node, cluster-autoscaler should spin up a replacement but we must account for capacity—some jobs are GPU heavy.

jin: concrete next steps I can take:
- adjust PromRules: use rate() and 2-tier alerts (warning/page)
- add recording rules to reduce CPU on queries
- add suppression rule around dcgm_driver_restarts_total spikes
- create a k8s replacement annotation and a small automation to taint+post issue in inventory repo

maria: can you drop a PR with the rule diffs? I'll review the thresholds (we tuned earlier for A100 vs V100). Remember to include `for:` values as strings in the YAML so alertmanager grouping behaves.

kevin: also add a Grafana dashboard panel visualizing job:gpu:xid_rate15m and dcgm_ecc_uncorrected_errors_total per GPU id. That helped us triage last week.

ashley: FYI — while tuning, set severity=warning for ECC corrected spikes; only escalate uncorrected ECC to page. Corrected errors can be a sign of thermal issues, but not always immediate replacement.

jin: will open a PR and a one-pager with the runbook steps (cordon/drain command example):
```bash
kubectl cordon gpu-12
kubectl drain gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
```
Add label `redwood/replace=true` to nodes flagged for ops to pick up.

ops-bot: note: queued replacement ticket #INF-4321 created for gpu-12 (automated from tag).

maria: thanks — ping me once the PR is up and I'll test the alert noise reduction in staging. :pray:
